why: EVIDENCE: Canary 1.1 served 2384 of 9788 requests (~24%) with 0 5xx, identical to stable's 0/7404 (0.00% err on both). Latency is at parity on every endpoint: /browse p50/p95 22/27 (canary) vs 22/27 (stable); /search 47/60 vs 47/59; /checkout 79/102 vs 82/103 - the canary is marginally FASTER on the checkout path. The 4x30s windows show flat canary p95 (95, 95, 92, 95) against stable (96, 93, 94, 97) with zero 5xx in every window, so there is no upward drift, no memory-leak/warmup-creep signature, and no sign of load-dependent degradation over the 120s test. ONE ANOMALY: canary /search p99 = 652ms vs stable 61ms (~10x), which also lifts the canary aggregate p99 to 172ms vs stable 104ms. JUDGEMENT: that p99 is computed over only 729 canary /search requests, so it is set by roughly the 7 slowest calls (~1% of one endpoint). Because canary /search p50 (47ms) and p95 (60ms) are unchanged versus stable, the body of the distribution did not move - this is a small set of outliers, not a regression, and is most consistent with cold-cache/JIT warmup on a single freshly started pod. Nothing in the data shows it worsening with time or load. RISK WEIGHING: the bad-promote cost here is bounded - worst case a fraction of a percent of search requests take ~0.65s, with no errors and no checkout impact - whereas rolling back on a ~7-request tail would block the release on the weakest signal on the dashboard. CAVEAT/WATCH: p99 at this sample size is statistically unstable and the canary only saw 25% of traffic, so promote with monitoring: after shifting to 100%, watch /search p99 for 15-30 min (now with ~4x the sample) and roll back immediately if /search p99 stays above ~200ms, if /search p95 rises above ~80ms, or if any 5xx appear.
